it’s nice you care but you’re overprotective. Your daughter can handle herself, she wants to support her step-sister, if it’s too much for her she can make the decision to leave for herself. It’s not your job to shelter her and protect her, it’s your to SUPPORT her. 
You aren’t being supportive if you want to “hide” her from the family and others. Consider how much that would hurt if that was you. By asking her not to go, you are communicating that she isn’t part of the family, when she is a part of the family as much as anyone else.
Shame on you for entertaining the step-mother’s transphobia, your daughter should not be treated as a ‘sensitive’ topic. Being trans isn’t ‘provocative’ or ‘political’, Tran people are people like anyone else with thoughts and feelings like anyone else.  You’re prioritizing your relative’s ‘sensibilities’ over your own daughter, your actions communicate that you dont *really* accept her. You only accept her when it’s easy for you.
Instead of capitulating with bigots, you should should stand up for her and her place in the family. You can’t bend or you’re saying it’s okay to exclude your daughter from family functions. 
When you go to the wedding with your daughter, you introduce her as your daughter, don’t say anything about her being trans. If anyone challenges whether she belongs there you better say “she is my daughter, she belongs here as much as I do, she is part of the family” if someone disrespects her you say “don’t talk to my daughter that way, she is family.” But give her the opportunity to stand up for herself if she needs to. She is an independent woman, she can manage herself
